Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16
February, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 71
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 36819 of 2022
Applicant :- Jashbir Singh And Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Lal Mani Singh,Praveen Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sharique Ahmed Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and perused the record.

By means of this Application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the applicants have prayed to quash order dated 05.08.2021 passed by the Session Judge Kanpur Nagar and order dated 07.10.2020 passed by the Additional Session Judge, Court No.22, Kanpur Nagar both in Session Trial No.284 of 2018,
State Vs. Pavneet Gandhi and others, arising out of Case Crime No.9 of 2018, under Sections 498A,
304B, 323 I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kohna, District Kanpur Nagar.
As per facts mentioned in the FIR, the son of the applicants Pavneet Gandhi and sister of opposite party no.2 Jasleen Kaur were married on 27.11.2011, wherein apart from other gifts, Rs. 10,00,000/-
cash were also given, but after few months of the marriage Pavneet Gandhi, his father Jashbir Singh,
mother Smt. Ladi and brother Raja started demanding a honda city car and Rs. 25,00,000/- to extend the business.

entities.text: Additional Session Judge, Court No.22, Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Jasleen was taunted, thrashed, physically and mentally tortured at the hands of the applicants.
They did not consider the request of opposite party no.2.
On 25.12.2017, after snatching the entire jewellery and other stuff of Jasleen, she was sent back to her parental house by her parents-in-law and husband.
Somehow the matter was pacified and she was sent back to her in-laws house on 14.01.2018 alongwith her five year old son.
In the night of 19th January, 2018 Jaslin gave 2-3 rings to her mother regarding her extreme torture at the hands of her in-laws.

On 20th January 2018 by facebook, it was brought into the knowledge of opposite party no.2 and his family members that due to this mental torture as a consequence of demand of dowry of her in-laws Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: including husband, Jasleen committed suicide by jumping from Ganga Bairaj Bridge.

A suicide audio was found in the mobile of the deceased, wherein she mentioned that "in all her senses she is committing suicide reason behind this suicide is only her mother-in-law and father-in-law, she wants to live with Mikku (her husband), but neither she is able to live with him nor she could live with him nor she can leave him, hence without any other reason she is committing suicide".

On the basis of this suicide note husband Pavneet Gandhi @ Mikku, who was arrested on 21.08.2018 was granted bail on 19.09.2018 and the further proceedings of his case were stayed, this stay is continuing till date.
After investigation, name of the brother-in-law Raja, who lives in CANADA was exonerated by the investigating officer.
Charge-sheet under Sections 498A, 304B, 323 I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kohna, District Kanpur Nagar was filed against the parents-in-law and husband of the deceased.

entities.text: Police Station Kohna, District Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As the case of the husband of the deceased was stayed by this Court, so the case of Jasbir and Smt. Laldi, the present applicants proceeded.

Further,
after recording the complete prosecution evidence the statements of six defence witnesses have also been recorded.

Before recording the defence evidence, the present applicants moved an application paper no. 77 Kha before the trial court that one day prior to the incident i.e. on 19.01.2016 Pavneet Gandhi, the husband of the deceased had a talk with his mother-in-law Paramjeet Kaur on mobile, but in that conversation there was no whisper of demand of dowry or harassment thereon, so the permission was sought to prove C.D. appended with the file by comparing the sample voice of Paramjeet Kaur with the alleged voice of Paramjeet Kaur in the conversation present in the C.D.
The prayer was made to take voice sample of Paramjeet Kaur.
This application was rejected vide order dated 05.08.2021 of the trial court, wherein the trial court opined that the case was fixed for defence evidence.

The statement of Smt. Paramjeet Kaur was recorded as PW-3 and the full opportunity was given to the accused to cross-examine that witness,
so no sufficient ground was found to summon Paramjeet Kaur for giving sample of her voice.

After recording the statements of the six defence witnesses, again an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. being paper no.112 Kha was moved by the present applicants in the trial court with the version that during defence evidence as DW-2 Pavneet Singh Gandhi, the husband of the deceased,
filed a list of documents in defence in the court on 06.10.2021 including one audio C.D. regarding telephonic conversation of Smt. Paramjeet Kaur and accused Pavneet Gandhi on 19.01.2018.

It was further averted that on 19.01.2018 from 12:53:06 531 second conversation was made between Pavneet Gandhi and Smt. Paramjeet Kaur and the voice of Paramjeet Kaur recorded in audio C.D.
the conversation in Punjabi and its translation in Hindi both are present on record.

In her cross-examination as PW-3 Smt. Paramjeet Kaur has accepted the telephonic conversation with her son-in-law on 19.01.2018, but in that conversation there is no mention of demand of a honda city car or Rs. 25,00,000/- to grow the business of Pavneet Singh Gandhi.
Thus, the forensic examination of the voice of Paramjeet Kaur recorded in audio C.D. was prayed to be done and the prayer was also made to take the voice sample of Paramjeet Kaur.

At the same time, prayer was also Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23783140/
2 made to let the audio C.D. be recited to Paramjeet Kaur so that she could accept or reject her voice in the CD.

entities.text: Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If she accepts that voice to be her own then there is no need of voice examination of Paramjeet Kaur, but if she denies the voice being her own in the audio C.D. then in the interest of justice the sample of the voice of Paramjeet Kaur be taken to compare it with the voice of conversation recorded in the audio C.D.

This application was rejected by the trial court vide order dated 07.10.2022 on the ground that on the application dated 07.11.2019 of Panveet Gandhi addressed to S.S.P., Kanpur Nagar, further investigation was done by second investigating officer Manoj Kumar Gupta and call detail report of the mobile of Panveet Gandhi and Paramjeet Kaur from 19.01.2018 to 21.01.2018 was prepared.
The papers of the subsequent case diary and call detail report were filed in the court on 13.08.2019.
The court concerned found that the case was fixed for defence evidence continuously from 05.08.2021 and defence had produced six witnesses.
Paramjeet Kaur had been extensively cross-examined as PW-3 by the accused counsel as her cross-examination ended in 20 pages.
At that time neither audio C.D. was presented by Panveet Singh nor Paramjeet Kaur was examined in that regard.

Previously also, on the same ground application paper no.77 Kha of the applicants had been rejected, again on the same ground, second application was not found considerable, hence, the same was rejected Against both the said orders dated 05.08.2021 and 07.10.2022, the present application under section 482 Cr.P.C has been moved by the applicants with a prayer to quash these orders and to give them an opportunity to get the voice sample of Paramjeet Kaur and get the sample compared with the voice available in the conversation claimed to be of Paramjeet Kaur in the audio C.D. filed in defence.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 opposed the application by filing counter affidavit and submitted that if out of 4-5 conversations, only 3 conversations are placed before the court by the applicants, it is not necessary that in every conversation the complaint of demand of dowry and harassment thereon be mentioned.
Sufficient ocular and circumstantial evidence against the applicants is on the record.
In suicide note also there is no mention of demand of dowry and the harassment thereon.
The original device mobile phone which is prerequisite has not been placed before the court.

Admittedly, audio C.D. has been prepared by co-accused Panveet Singh Gandhi,
the husband of the deceased, on the basis of conversation saved in his mobile phone.
In the trial court, the case is fixed for arguments, the applicants only want to gain time.

The application of the applicants is allowed or rejected would not make much difference because the demand of dowry or harassment on the basis of demand cannot be decided on the basis of audio C.D. only.
The child of the couple is also with his maternal uncle because in a writ of Habeas Corpus by Pavneet Singh, the child was not handed over to him, being him the accused of the case.
Though, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that against that Single Bench order, Division Bench has remanded back the case for fresh decision.

It is also submitted that after these two applications one more application being application paper no. 123 Kha under Section 294 Cr.P.C. was moved by the present applicants and prayer was made that this audio CD be recited to Paramjeet Kaur and she must be asked about the authenticity of the voice in that audio C.D.

This application was again rejected by the Additional District Judge, Court Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23783140/
3 no.22, Kanpur Nagar on the ground that since 05.08.2021, the case was pending for defence evidence and statements of seven defence witnesses had been recorded.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Court Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Since last many days the accused persons had not filed defence evidence, but with a view to prolong the proceedings one or other application is being moved by them.
Last opportunity was given to the accused persons but no more oral or documentary evidence had been produced by the accused persons.

As this Court had directed the trial court to decide the case in a time bound period, so the trial court rejected this application paper no.123 Kha moved under 294 Cr.P.C. and closed the opportunity of defence evidence of the applicants and fixed 16.02.2023 for final arguments.
Photocopy of this order dated 04.02.2023 is placed before the Court and it is submitted that attempts are being made by the applicants to somehow delay the case.
This is the frivolous application, the applications with the same prayer of the applicants have been rejected by the trial court thrice.
Thus, prayer is made to reject the present application.

From the above facts, it is clear that three applications were moved by the applicants with the prayer for taking the voice sample of Paramjeet Kaur, the mother of the deceased and to send it for examination for comparing it with the voice of the conversation present in audio C.D. placed before the Court by the applicants alleging the conversation present in the C.D. to be of Paramjeet Kaur and Pavneet Singh.
All these applications were rejected by the trial court mainly on the ground that the case was fixed for defence evidence.
The statement of Paramjeet Kaur was recorded as PW-3 and the applicants had full opportunity to cross-examine Paramjeet Kaur regarding the C.D., Paramjeet Kaur was extensively cross-

examined by the accused counsel and by finding that the applicants were prolonging the case, at last, the opportunity of the applicants of producing rest defence evidence was closed by the trial court and the case was fixed for arguments.
Only orders dated 05.08.2021 and 07.10.2022 have been challenged before this Court.

However,
order on application paper no.123 Kha, under Section 294 Cr.P.C., which was rejected vide order dated 04.02.2023 has not been challenged before this Court.

It is an admitted fact that both the applications paper no.77 Kha, dated 05.08.2021 and application paper no.112 Kha, dated 17.09.2022 were rejected vide orders dated 05.08.2021 and 07.10.2022,
respectively, at the stage, when the case was fixed for defence evidence.

At the stage of defence evidence, when C.D. is said to have filed or otherwise also, if it was on record filed by the investigating officer alongwith other documents, even then the defence had a right to give his defence, either by producing oral witnesses or by producing documentary evidence or by producing electronic devices like C.D. etc.

If the applicants have given an audio C.D. in their defence, the applicants had a right to prove that C.D. What would be the evidentiary value of this secondary evidence, if the primary evidence (mobile phone) was not taken into possession by the investigating officer or it was not produced by the applicants in the court, is to be seen by the trial court at the time of arguments/ judgment.

An opportunity had been given to the applicants at the stage of prosecution evidence to cross-examine prosecution witness PW-3 Paramjeet Kaur, hence now the defence could not be given an opportunity to prove C.D. place by them in defence in the trial court is an erroneous view, because at the time of defence evidence, it is the right of the accused persons to produce and prove the documents whatever they have produced in the court and whichever, they want to prove.

The finding that the applications were moved at a belated stage, just to prolong the Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23783140/
4 proceedings, is again finding against the law, because it is only at the stage of defence evidence, that the accused persons, the present applicants, could produce their evidence and seek a permission to prove that evidence by means whatever they consider proper.

entities.text: Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As both the applications are moved at the time, when the case was still fixed for defence evidence, the applications by the applicants cannot be said to be moved at a belated stage or with a view to prolong the proceedings.
Hence, the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. of the applicants is allowed.
Orders dated 05.08.2021 and 07.10.2022 of the trial court are hereby set aside.
Both these applications paper no.77 Kha and 112 Kha are allowed.
The trial court is directed to award an opportunity to the applicants to get the audio C.D. filed by them in defence evidence proved, by producing/ taking voice of the sample of Paramjeet Kaur.
The trial court is further directed to summon Paramjeet Kaur to accept or deny her voice in the audio C.D. produced by the applicants.
If Paramjeet Kaur refuses the voice in C.D. to be her own, then to get the voice of conversation in C.D. to be compared with the voice sample taken from Paramjeet Kaur at the expense of applicants.

So far as the objection of opposite party no.2 is concerned, that out of various conversation only 2-3 conversations have been produced by the applicants by way of audio C.D., the opposite party no.2 shall be free to produce and get prove the rest conversation, which may be still present in the mobile of Paramjeet Kaur.

Order Date :- 16.2.2023 Radhika  Jashbir Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23783140/
